rule: Address the player directly in the active voice
do: Pay $1 to gain 2 resources.
dont: The player pays $1 to gain 2 resources.
source: What Makes a Great Rulebook? – Stonemaier Games

rule: Use passive voice only for universal prohibitions
do: Mountain tiles cannot be removed from the map.
dont: Players may not remove mountain tiles from the map.
source: Board Game Editing Style Guide (Michael "Curby" Lee)

rule: Pick 2nd or 3rd person and stay consistent within a section
do: Each player reveals 1 card from their hand.
dont: Mixing 'you move 3 pieces' and 'the player may move fewer'.
source: Board Game Editing Style Guide (Michael "Curby" Lee)

rule: Singular they; 'that player' when 'they' is ambiguous
do: If a player has no Scientists, that player may not research Technologies.
dont: he / she / (s)he / s/he / he or she / him or her
source: Board Game Editing Style Guide (Michael "Curby" Lee)

rule: may = optional; may not = forbidden; cannot = impossible; must = compelled
do: If the active player cannot play a card, they must draw a card instead.
dont: Using 'should' anywhere in rules text.
source: Board Game Editing Style Guide (Michael "Curby" Lee)

rule: gain (unlimited supply) vs take (limited supply or from a player) vs give
do: At the end of each round, gain $5.
dont: Using 'take' for something from the general supply.
source: The Stonemaier Games Style Guide

rule: Trigger/condition first, effect second
do: If you roll a 5 or higher, draw a card.
dont: Draw a card if you roll a 5 or higher.
source: Board Game Editing Style Guide (Michael "Curby" Lee)

rule: One action per sentence; the one-breath test
do: Choose one area of the Spaceship. In that area, add damage tokens equal to...
dont: A single sentence with a parenthetical list plus a calculation.
source: How to Write a Rulebook for Your Board Game – Entro Games

rule: when (once/predictable) / whenever (repeatable) / if (may never happen) / at (point in time)
do: Whenever a player draws a card, ...
dont: Using 'when' for something that may never occur.
source: Board Game Editing Style Guide (Michael "Curby" Lee)

rule: each (individually) vs every / all (as a group)
do: Each card is scored according to its Infamy stat.
dont: 'Every card scores' when each scores separately.
source: Board Game Editing Style Guide (Michael "Curby" Lee)

rule: less for singular nouns, fewer for plural; greater/less than for numbers, higher/lower for dice
do: If you roll a 4 or higher...
dont: Mixing 'greater than' and 'higher' for the same comparison type.
source: Board Game Editing Style Guide (Michael "Curby" Lee)

rule: turn < round < act/season; phases and steps subdivide
do: Each player's turn consists of a Draw Phase, an Auction Phase and a Building Phase.
dont: Using 'phase' at two different levels in the same game.
source: Board Game Editing Style Guide (Michael "Curby" Lee)

rule: Hyphenate face-up / face-down consistently
do: Shuffle the cards into a face-down deck.
dont: 'Flip the top card of each deck face down under it' (ambiguous).
source: BGG blog: Writing Rules – facing up to breaking the rules (Andy Van Zandt)

rule: One die type: 'a die'. Multiple sizes: 4d12 notation. Consider 'dice' for both numbers
do: Roll 4d12 and place each die on a different runway.
dont: Alternating die/dice unpredictably within one book.
source: Board Game Editing Style Guide (Michael "Curby" Lee)

rule: Capitalise only specific in-game components, actions and values
do: Gain 5 Gold from the central supply.
dont: Capitalising Every Important-Looking Noun.
source: Board Game Editing Style Guide (Michael "Curby" Lee)

rule: Bold = keywords/headings. Italic = examples, captions, flavour. No underline. No long all-caps
do: Bold the keyword where it is first defined.
dont: Underlined rules text; ALL CAPS paragraphs.
source: Board Game Editing Style Guide (Michael "Curby" Lee)

rule: Digits for game quantities; spell out flavour numbers and sentence-initial numbers
do: Two dice may be placed on each territory.
dont: '2 dice may be placed...' at the start of a sentence.
source: The Stonemaier Games Style Guide

rule: Numbered = sequence. Bulleted = unordered options. Periods only on full sentences
do: 1. Shuffle the deck. 2. Deal 5 cards to each player.
dont: Numbered labels on a diagram (readers misread them as quantities).
source: Board Game Editing Style Guide (Michael "Curby" Lee)

rule: Serial (Oxford) comma; one space after a period; double quotes
do: Farmers, Merchants, and Tailors
dont: Two spaces after a period.
source: The Stonemaier Games Style Guide

rule: Short clarifications only — never new rules
do: Each player may deploy two Infantry Units (but not other types of units).
dont: Parenthetical that introduces a rule found nowhere else.
source: Board Game Editing Style Guide (Michael "Curby" Lee)

rule: Expand acronyms on first use in the rulebook (and optionally per section)
do: Energy Production Rate (EPR)
dont: Multiple visually-similar acronyms: CWC vs CWL.
source: Board Game Editing Style Guide (Michael "Curby" Lee)

rule: Cite the target of any cross-reference
do: see Connections, p. 34
dont: 'See above' / 'as previously mentioned'.
source: Board Game Editing Style Guide (Michael "Curby" Lee)

rule: Treat 'exception', 'remember' and 'should' as design smells
do: Remove or redesign the exception.
dont: Shipping a rule whose only home is an exception clause.
source: The Stonemaier Games Style Guide

rule: A 'mat' belongs to a player; a 'board' is shared
do: Place your workers on your player mat.
dont: Calling the shared board a mat, or vice versa.
source: The Stonemaier Games Style Guide

rule: Choose names that start with different letters, especially for sibling headings
do: Dockyards / Assembly
dont: Shipyards / Shipbuilding as sibling headings.
source: Board Game Editing Style Guide (Michael "Curby" Lee)

rule: Delete filler and condescension
do: The victory condition is to destroy all other castles.
dont: 'The victory condition is simply to destroy...'
source: BGG: Rules Writing 101 (with an example)
